Active Learning

SPARC uses a Query-by-Committee (QbC) strategy to select which structures to send for DFT labelling. An ensemble of num_models independently trained models is used; configurations where the models disagree are the most informative for improving the potential.

Force Deviation Thresholds

The key tuning parameters are in the model_dev block:

model_dev:
  f_min_dev: 0.1    # eV/Å — lower bound
  f_max_dev: 0.8    # eV/Å — upper bound

The outcome for each frame depends on its maximum atomic force deviation across the model committee:

Deviation range

Outcome

Below f_min_dev

Model is confident — frame discarded (already well described)

Between bounds

Selected as candidate for DFT labelling

Above f_max_dev

Model has no knowledge — frame discarded (likely unphysical)

Typical starting values: f_min_dev: 0.05–0.1 eV/Å, f_max_dev: 0.3–0.8 eV/Å. Tighten the range in later iterations as the model matures.

Committee Evaluation Backend

model_dev.qbc picks how force deviation across the committee is computed. Two backends produce the same 8-column model_dev_N.out format (step, max_devi_e, min_devi_f, max_devi_f, avg_devi_f, ...) that feeds the thresholds above — only the evaluation path differs.

model_dev:
  qbc: "internal"    # "internal" (default) or "deepmd"

qbc

How it evaluates

Framework support

"internal" (default)

In-process: one batched DeepPot.eval call per committee member for the whole trajectory.

DeepMD only

"deepmd"

Converts the trajectory to DeePMD npy format with dpdata and shells out to the dp model-devi CLI.

DeepMD only

"internal" skips the dpdata → npy conversion and the dp subprocess entirely. Its deviation formulas match dp model-devi and deepmd-kit’s own calc_model_devi_{f,v,e} exactly — verified against dp model-devi output to the float32 noise floor (~1e-6).

Note

The underlying sparc.src.utils.model_qbc.compute_model_devi() also has an ASE-calculator-loop path for nequip, allegro and mace committees, and a configurable device. Neither is reachable yet through model_dev.qbc — the only call site (active_learning.py:QueryByCommittee) hardcodes compute_model_devi(trajfile, model_names, "deepmd", "cuda", outfile). Multi-framework support needs that call wired to the model’s actual framework before it is usable from input.yaml.

Note

Universal models with frame parameters (fparam, e.g. DPA-3) are handled differently by each backend. "deepmd" reads the model’s default_fparam and writes it explicitly into the fparam.npy of every converted data set. "internal" has no such write step — for these models DeepPot.eval falls back to the model’s own baked-in default fparam instead.

Number of Models

mlip_setup.num_models controls committee size. A minimum of 2 is required; 4 is recommended for reliable uncertainty estimates. More models increase training cost but improve candidate selection quality.

Restarting an Interrupted Run

SPARC writes a progress.json file after every DFT candidate in Step 1 of each AL iteration. If the workflow crashes — during training, ML-MD, or mid-DFT — set learning_restart: true to resume automatically:

active_learning: true
learning_restart: true

latest_model is deprecated and ignored. The model used for ML-MD is always auto-detected from the current iteration’s training directory (iter_N/01.train) after retraining completes. It can be omitted.

SPARC reads progress.json to determine which AL iteration was in progress and how many candidates had been labelled, then:

  1. Re-runs the last DFT candidate (minor redundancy — identical result).

  2. Retrains models from the combined trajectory.

  3. Runs ML-MD with the freshly retrained models for that iteration.

Note

progress.json is only updated during the DFT labelling step. A crash during ML-MD causes a restart from the beginning of that iteration’s DFT labelling — already-labelled candidates are re-processed from the last saved index.

Restart Exploration

By default, every active-learning iteration seeds ML-MD from the input structure. With restart_exploration: true, iteration ≥ 1 draws its initial geometry from the QbC candidate pool of the previous iteration:

iter_{N-1}/02.dpmd/dft_candidates/candidates.extxyz

What is a QbC candidate?

After ML-MD, SPARC evaluates each trajectory frame with Query-by-Committee (QbC): an ensemble of models predicts atomic forces and their spread (force deviation) is recorded. Per frame:

Force deviation

Outcome

Below f_min_dev

Models agree – frame discarded (already learned)

Within [f_min_dev, f_max_dev]

Kept as candidate – moderate disagreement, worth labeling

Above f_max_dev

Models diverge catastrophically – discarded (likely unphysical)

Surviving frames are scanned by the RMSD filter and stored in candidates.extxyz. This list contains locally distinct, and model-uncertain configurations along the MD trajectory.

Why restart from the QbC pool?

Without restart exploration, every iteration begins from the same input geometry. The model keeps re-sampling the same region of phase space. Seeding from the QbC pool directs each new ML-MD run outward from configurations the committee already flagged as uncertain but not yet fully learned.

Configuration

mlip_setup:
  restart_exploration: false   # Seed from QbC pool [Optional, Default: false]
  restart_frame: "candidates"  # Selection strategy [Optional, Default: "candidates"]

Selection strategies

All three modes read from the same QbC pool. They differ in how parallel MD shoots (multiple_run) are mapped to pool entries:

restart_frame

Behaviour

"candidates"

Round-robin (default). Shoot k → candidate k mod N. Each parallel trajectory seeds from a different pool entry; the list wraps when multiple_run > N. Deterministic. Recommended for multiple_run > 1.

"last"

All shoots seed from the final pool entry – the most recently flagged uncertain configuration. Suitable for multiple_run: 1.

"random"

Stochastic resampling. Each shoot draws a uniform random entry from the pool. The same frame may seed multiple trajectories.

Worked example

Suppose iteration 1 produces five QbC candidates [A, B, C, D, E]. Iteration 2 runs with restart_exploration: true and multiple_run: 4:

restart_frame

Shoot assignments

Notes

"candidates"

1→A, 2→B, 3→C, 4→D

Systematic coverage of the shortlist

"last"

1→E, 2→E, 3→E, 4→E

All continue from the same geometry

"random"

1→C, 2→A, 3→C, 4→E

Draws may repeat (e.g. shoots 1 and 3 both → C)

Note

Active from iteration 1 onward. Falls back to the input structure if candidates.extxyz is absent.

DEAL: Sparse GP Diversity Filter

After the QbC force-deviation gate, a second filter removes redundant candidates before DFT labelling. By default this uses a geometric RMSD check (Kabsch algorithm). When deal.enabled: true, the geometric filter is replaced by a Sparse Gaussian Process (SGP) posterior-variance filter operating in ACE descriptor space.

Note

SPARC targets DEAL >= 3.0, which carries its own native sparse-GP extension (FlareConfig was renamed SGPConfig). Older DEAL releases are refused with a warning and the run falls back to the RMSD filter.

Mathematical Foundation

Local environment descriptors (B2 / ACE). Each atom \(i\) in a candidate frame is mapped to a descriptor vector \(\mathbf{d}_i \in \mathbb{R}^{n_\mathrm{feat}}\) by the Atomic Cluster Expansion B2 basis:

\[B_i^{nl} = \sum_{j \in \mathcal{N}(i)} R_n(r_{ij})\, Y_l(\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{ij})\]

where \(R_n\) are Chebyshev radial basis functions up to order nmax, \(Y_l\) are real spherical harmonics up to degree lmax, and \(\mathcal{N}(i)\) denotes neighbours within the cutoff radius. Descriptors are normalised by the NormalizedDotProduct kernel with hyper-parameters \(\sigma=2\) and power \(p=2\):

\[K(\mathbf{d}, \mathbf{d}') = \sigma^2 \left(\frac{\mathbf{d} \cdot \mathbf{d}'} {|\mathbf{d}||\mathbf{d}'|}\right)^p\]

Sparse Gaussian Process. Given a set of inducing-point descriptors \(\mathbf{Z} = \{\mathbf{d}_1, \ldots, \mathbf{d}_M\}\) accumulated from selected frames, the SGP posterior variance for a new local environment \(\mathbf{d}^*\) is:

\[\sigma^2(\mathbf{d}^*) = K(\mathbf{d}^*, \mathbf{d}^*) - \mathbf{k}^{\top}(\mathbf{d}^*)\, \mathbf{K}_{ZZ}^{-1}\, \mathbf{k}(\mathbf{d}^*)\]

where \(\mathbf{k}(\mathbf{d}^*) = [K(\mathbf{d}^*, \mathbf{d}_j)]_{j=1}^{M}\) is the cross-covariance vector and \(\mathbf{K}_{ZZ}\) is the \(M \times M\) kernel matrix over inducing points. A frame is selected when any of its atomic environments has variance above deal.threshold; upon selection its descriptors are added to \(\mathbf{Z}\) (expanding the inducing set for subsequent candidates).

This greedy sequential selection guarantees that no two selected frames share a novel environment — unlike RMSD, which is purely geometric and coordinate-frame-dependent.

Selection Modes

Threshold mode (default) makes one pass at a fixed deal.threshold. The number of surviving frames is whatever the trajectory happens to yield.

Budget mode (deal.max_selected: N) instead targets a frame count. It runs repeated passes over the candidates, lowering the threshold as \(f^{i+1}\) (threshold_factor, default 0.7) on pass \(i\), and stops as soon as N frames are collected or max_iterations passes are spent:

pass 1  threshold 0.700   pool 120 frames   →  4 selected
pass 2  threshold 0.490   pool 116 frames   →  9 selected
pass 3  threshold 0.343   pool 111 frames   → 20 selected   → budget reached

The same GP object is reused across passes (DEAL.configure_run), so the inducing set keeps growing and a frame rejected in pass 1 is re-judged against everything learned since. Already-selected frames leave the pool; from pass 2 on the remaining pool is shuffled so trajectory order does not bias which frames win the lowered threshold. Frames carry their trajectory index in info['original_frame'] so bookkeeping survives that shuffle.

Per-Atom Candidate Mask

deal.mask restricts GP evaluation to atoms flagged by a per-atom uncertainty array. Atoms outside the mask get uncertainty \(-1\), so they can neither trigger a selection nor enter the sparse set. On reactive, interface and defect systems — where a handful of atoms drive the chemistry and the rest are well-known bulk — this both cuts prediction time and stops thermal noise in the bulk from spending DFT slots.

The mask is derived from a per-atom array in frame.arrays:

Name

Level

Meaning

max_devi_f

frame (info)

Scalar QbC force deviation; drives the [f_min_dev, f_max_dev] gate

per_atom_devi_f

atom (arrays)

One force deviation per atom; source for the mask

deal_mask

atom (arrays)

Boolean eligibility array DEAL actually reads

Warning

SPARC does not produce per_atom_devi_f yet — it needs dp model-devi --atomic, which is not wired into QueryByCommittee(). Until it is, enable the mask only if you attach the array yourself; frames missing it disable masking with a warning instead of failing the run. Set deal.mask to a string to read a differently named array.

With mask_threshold unset, DEAL picks thresholds automatically: per frame, mask_fraction × frame_max (default 0.3), and frames whose maximum falls outside [1.1 × mean, 4.0 × mean] across the trajectory get an empty mask — those frames can then never be selected.

Data Flow Through the Pipeline

The figure below traces how array shapes transform at each stage.

dpmd.traj  (ASE binary, N frames, 3×n_at forces per frame)
    │
    ▼  dpdata.LabeledSystem  →  npy sets (coords, forces, energies)
    │
    ▼  dp model-devi  →  model_dev_K.out  (N rows × 4 columns)
       columns: step | max_devi_e | min_devi_f | max_devi_f
    │
    ▼  Force-deviation gate  [min_lim, max_lim]
       keeps C frames  (C << N)
       → candidates.extxyz  (C × (3n_at + 1) per frame)
    │
    ├──(RMSD path)──────────────────────────────────────────┐
    │  Kabsch RMSD vs. reference + accepted set             │
    │  drop if RMSD < rmsd_threshold                        │
    │  → candidates.extxyz  (C' ≤ C frames)                │
    └──(DEAL path)──────────────────────────────────────────┘
       attach_dummy_calc: zeros energy/forces on each frame
       DataConfig(images=C frames)
       SGPConfig: B2 descriptors, NDP kernel
           nmax × lmax  radial × angular channels
           cutoff auto-read from DeepMD input.json rcut
       optional mask: deal_mask marks eligible atoms
       DEAL.run():
           for each frame in order:
               compute d* for every eligible atom
               if max σ²(d*) > threshold:
                   select frame
                   add d* to inducing set Z
       budget mode: repeat with threshold ×= threshold_factor,
           same GP, pool minus already-selected frames
       → selected frames list  (S ≤ C frames)
    │
    ▼  CalculateDFTEnergy × S
       appends to  iter_N/00.dft/AseMD.traj

Array shapes at the DEAL stage (n_at = atoms per frame, C = QbC candidates):

Variable

Shape

Notes

candidate_frames

list[Atoms], length C

Each frame: positions (n_at, 3), symbols (n_at,)

B2 descriptor per atom

(n_feat,) where n_feat ≈ nmax × (lmax+1)²

Computed inside DEAL’s native sparse-GP extension (C++/pybind11)

Kernel matrix \(K_{ZZ}\)

(M, M) growing as frames are selected

Cholesky-updated in-place; \(M\) starts at 0

selected (output)

list[Atoms], length S ≤ C

Returned to QueryByCommittee; written to candidates.extxyz

Parallelization Constraints

DEAL’s SGP is sequential by design: each frame’s variance is evaluated against the inducing set built from all previously accepted frames. There is no embarrassingly parallel variant — the order of evaluation affects which frames are selected. Do not attempt to batch or shuffle candidate_frames before calling run_deal_filter.

DEAL’s native kernel evaluations are multi-threaded internally (OpenMP). The adapter caps threads at min(half the CPUs, 4) so the GP does not starve concurrent DFT jobs; override with advanced.omp_threads or by exporting OMP_NUM_THREADS before launching SPARC (an existing value always wins):

export OMP_NUM_THREADS=4
sparc -i input.yaml

MKL_THREADING_LAYER=GNU is set for the same reason as before: DEAL’s extension links Eigen, which compiles with EIGEN_USE_MKL_ALL whenever LAPACK resolves to MKL, and some conda builds ship an inconsistent libmkl_avx512.so that aborts at load.

The surrounding SPARC workflow (DFT labelling, DeepMD training) is single-process; parallelism there comes from MPI-parallel VASP / CP2K and the multi-GPU training launched by dp train.

Enabling DEAL

One line is enough:

deal:
  enabled: true

The full user-facing surface is five keys — everything else has a default:

Key

Default

Meaning

enabled

false

true → SGP filter; false → Kabsch RMSD filter

threshold

0.01

SGP posterior variance cut (threshold mode only)

max_selected

null

Set an integer to switch to budget mode and target that frame count

cutoff

null

Descriptor cutoff in Å; null auto-reads rcut / r_max

mask

false

true (or an array name) to restrict the GP to flagged atoms

deal.threshold is dimensionless SGP posterior variance in ACE descriptor space. It is not comparable to f_min_dev (eV/Å). Start at 0.01; lower values retain more frames, higher values are more aggressive. In budget mode it is ignored — the decaying threshold is used instead:

deal:
  enabled: true
  max_selected: 20    # 20 DFT calculations per AL iteration, no tuning

Advanced Options

The rest of the DEAL API lives under deal.advanced. Keys are routed to the object each belongs to and validated on entry, so a typo raises instead of being silently ignored:

deal:
  enabled: true
  max_selected: 20
  advanced:
    threshold_factor: 0.6       # faster decay → more frames per pass
    max_atoms_added: 0.1        # cap environments added per frame
    save_full_trajectory: true  # per-atom uncertainty for every frame

Group

Keys

Defaults

Notes

GP selection

update_threshold, max_atoms_added, min_steps_with_model, initial_atoms

null, 0.2, 1, null

update_threshold: null tracks 0.8 × threshold, so it keeps following the decay in budget mode

Descriptor

nmax, lmax, radial_basis, cutoff_function

8, 4, chebyshev, cosine

B2 basis size; cost grows as nmax × (lmax+1)²

Kernel

sigma, power

2.0, 2

NormalizedDotProduct hyper-parameters

GP

variance_type

local

local is the only value that keeps DEAL’s fast path

Mask

mask_threshold, mask_upper_threshold, mask_mode, mask_fraction, mask_plot

null, null, above, 0.3, false

Used only when deal.mask is set

Training/output

train_hyps, save_gp, save_full_trajectory, verbose

false, false, false, true

train_hyps and save_gp both disable the local-uncertainty fast path — expect a slower run

Budget/runtime

max_iterations, threshold_factor, seed, omp_threads

10, 0.7, 24, null

Handled by SPARC’s budget loop, not passed to DEAL

threshold, max_selected, cutoff and mask are rejected inside advanced — they belong at the top level.

Extra output files land next to candidates.extxyz: deal_selected.xyz always, plus deal_sgp.json (save_gp), deal_trajectory_uncertainty.xyz with a per-atom atomic_uncertainty array (save_full_trajectory) and deal_mask.png (mask_plot: true).

To disable (default), omit the block or set enabled: false — the RMSD filter is active:

model_dev:
  rmsd_threshold: 0.025   # Å — RMSD filter used when DEAL is off
